mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically precedes economic slowdown and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market contraction, which is a strong negative signal for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.12% and CPIAUCSL rising above 235.2), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS > 0.12 and CPIAUCSL > 235.2, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900 signals a weakening housing market, which is a negative indicator for the broader economy and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 900, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 440,000 signals weak consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS falls below 440000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.12% signals an early monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.12, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
